subject: Implementation playbook: non-consumptive processing & transfer gating
messages:
From: Elena Marton <elena@carebridge.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: operational playbook + proof of non-training handling

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the conversation earlier this week. Procurement and Legal at Carebridge have a few explicit asks before we can finalize the DPA amendment that includes the 'no-training / no-model-improvement' commitment:

- An ops playbook showing how Redwood enforces non-consumptive processing at request- and tenant-level (labeling/flags, KV cache scoping, retention rules).
- A list of subprocessors involved in telemetry, monitoring, and backups, and an explanation of their scoping.
- Export/escrow mechanics: what data artifacts you can provide (SFTP export, manifests, audit logs) and a sample timeline for a 3rd-party audit.
- KMS residency and whether customer keys can be used for any transfer lanes.

Can you share a one-page summary and any supporting artifacts today? Procurement needs items to justify the procurement committee review next Tuesday.

Attachments: carebridge-rfp-appendix.pdf (from Carebridge)

Best,
Elena
Elena Marton
Senior Procurement Manager, Carebridge Health

From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-19T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: operational playbook + proof of non-training handling

Elena — thanks, we can do this. Internal team: tagging for visibility.

Plan I propose:
1) Share a concise "non-consumptive operations" playbook (one page executive + 4-page appendix) that covers flags, routing, and retention.
2) Provide a subprocessor inventory and the minimal scoping statements for telemetry/backups.
3) Offer an SFTP export manifest example + an escrow timeline (we can stage a sample export within 48 hours).
4) Confirm KMS options — we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own) for onshore export lanes; note any constraints.

David — can you attach a technical outline and the SFTP manifest template?
Kimberly — can you review the language we should include in the playbook about proof artifacts and acceptable audit evidence (SOC2 excerpt, export receipts)?
Marissa — procurement timeline / any billing/contract notes we should flag for the deal team?

I'll assemble the one-page summary and the appendix. Attaching: nonconsumptive-playbook-v1.pdf (DRAFT).

Thanks,
Mina
Director, Privacy & Product Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-19T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: operational playbook + proof of non-training handling

Mina / team — attaching the operational artifacts. Highlights below.

Attachment: sftp-escrow-ops.xlsx (stub) — contains:
- Export manifest schema (tenant_id, time_window, object_counts, md5 checksums).
- SFTP export runbook (roles, required approvals, retention of export artifacts).
- Audit trail sample (log entries showing export job IDs and checksums).

Technical notes:
- Non-consumptive flagging: requests labeled at route time (X-Redwood-No-Train: true) and recorded in the request index. Flag persists in request metadata and is used to short-circuit model update pipelines and telemetry forwarding.
- KV/Prefix caching: tenant-scoped caches are isolated; KV eviction follows the retention TTL applied to flagged requests.
- Telemetry: we redact prompt text from sampling telemetry and only retain minimal metrics for SLOs; we can provide sampling receipts that show redaction.
- KMS: we support customer-managed keys in our EU and US onshore lanes; if Carebridge requires BYOK for exports, we can generate an export package encrypted with the provided key.

I can run a dry export in our staging tenant and produce a sample manifest + signed checksum by EOD tomorrow if that helps procurement.

-David
David Kim
Director, Infrastructure 
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-19T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: operational playbook + proof of non-training handling

Team — quick legal checklist to ensure the artifacts meet contracting:

- Playbook language: must clearly state that 'no-training' is an enforceable request flag and describe the scope (all model training, fine-tuning, online adaptation). Avoid ambiguous wording like 'model updates' without definition.
- Evidence types: procurement typically accepts: export manifests with checksums, signed audit logs for the relevant window, and a short certification letter from our Security team. SOC2 excerpt is helpful but not sufficient alone for the DPA amendment.
- Subprocessors: include names + roles + country of data processing, and each must be tied to a minimal-purpose statement (e.g., "monitoring — error rates only, no prompt storage").
- SLA/timelines: state maximum turnaround for producing export artifacts (we should commit to 5 business days for standard requests and 2 business days for urgent remediation with escalation).

I'll draft the legal paragraph we can drop into the appendix and produce a certification template. Mina, I'd tweak the playbook appendix to use explicit terms: 'no-train flag', 'non-consumptive processing', 'export manifest'.

-Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Legal (Data & Privacy)
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Marton <elena@carebridge.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@carebridge.com
Date: 2026-08-19T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: operational playbook + proof of non-training handling

Mina,

Appreciate the quick turnaround and level of detail. The playbook and the ops artifacts sound like exactly what procurement needs. Two quick asks before we move to legal review:

1) Can you send a one-page executive summary (suitable for our procurement committee packet) that includes: what proof artifacts we'll receive, the export timeline, and the commitment language you propose for the DPA?
2) Can you confirm the 5 business day SLA for standard export requests and whether Carebridge can request BYOK-encrypted export packages?

If we get that by EOD Monday our committee will have enough to proceed to legal redlines.

Thanks — looking forward to the one-pager.

Best,
Elena
